docs.title: MusicBee Tagger MCP
docs.text:
MusicBee Tagger MCP is a local stdio MCP server for investigating and proposing audio metadata corrections. It reads audio metadata, searches and verifies MusicBrainz candidates, and stages proposals for review.

The MCP server never writes audio files. It also exposes no MCP tool that accepts playlist or audio paths. Run the local registration command yourself in a separate PowerShell window and give the agent only its returned tokens. Only the separate musicbee-tagger-apply CLI can apply staged changes, after interactive user confirmation, and it creates backups by default.

This keeps paths out of chat and MCP request/response payloads. It is not a Windows security boundary: an agent with unrestricted local shell access as your Windows user could inspect the registration files. Use the cleanup command after the investigation; use a separately isolated service account if that stronger threat model is required.

docs.title: Windows desktop release
docs.text:
The release bundle includes a Python wheel, source distribution, Windows installer, Claude Code MCP configuration, and Claude Code plugin archive with the model-invocable musicbee-investigator skill. The installer defaults to:

  • Application and virtual environment: K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\
  • Launchers: K:\bin\
  • Private stage data: K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\data\staged\
  • Private registration data: K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\data\registered\
  • Persistent batch-operation queue: K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\data\queue\

The data directory is separate from the installed environment so package upgrades do not replace pending proposals, local registrations, or the shared batch-operation queue. The installer preserves existing data. Back up the data directory to preserve them. Queue items persist until their status is updated; there is no automatic cleanup.

MCP agents connected to the same configured data directory share the durable operation queue across server restarts. Use enqueue_batch_operation to add path-free work, list_batch_operations to query it by status or batch, and update_batch_operation to record progress. Queue items remain available until their status is updated; all agents using the same data directory see the same queue.

To install directly from a source checkout without downloading or extracting a release bundle, run this from the repository root:

.\install.ps1

This builds a wheel from the checkout in a temporary directory and passes it to the same installer used by the release bundle. Python 3 and the Windows py launcher are required. Override the default application and launcher directories if needed:

.\install.ps1 -InstallRoot "D:\Apps\MusicBeeTagger" -BinRoot "D:\Tools\bin"

Alternatively, download and extract a Windows release bundle, then run its installer while supplying the included wheel:

.\install.ps1 -WheelPath .\musicbee_tagger_mcp-0.4.5-py3-none-any.whl

Before upgrading an existing installation, close MCP clients using the server. If installed MusicBee Tagger processes are running, the installer asks to close them. If a process has no closable window or does not exit, it offers to terminate it before continuing. Save any work in those processes first. The installer also removes stale ~usicbee-tagger-mcp* pip leftovers from the dedicated environment after interrupted upgrades.

docs.title: Shared batch queue
docs.text: All MCP clients using the same configured data directory share a durable, SQLite-backed queue. Agents can add path-free operations with enqueue_batch_operation, query by batch and status with list_batch_operations, and record progress with update_batch_operation. Queue entries are retained across server restarts and package upgrades; include no local audio or playlist paths in titles or details.

docs.title: Docker Hosting & Two-Container Sandboxing
docs.text:
For containerized deployments, MusicBee Tagger MCP provides a secure, least-privilege Docker Compose setup (docker-compose.yml) utilizing a two-container architecture:

  • musicbee-mcp: Runs the HTTPS MCP server with a read-only root file system, outbound network restricted to MusicBrainz/ACRCloud APIs, and the audio library mounted strictly read-only (:ro) to guarantee the MCP server and AI agent can never modify audio files.
  • musicbee-apply: An isolated offline apply agent with no network access and read-write access to the audio library (:rw), responsible solely for executing review-approved stage manifests.

For full setup instructions, see Docker Hosting Guide.

docs.title: Artist split validation (agent-assisted)
docs.text: The agent loop exposes four read-only tools for splitting malformed artist fields: propose_artist_split (mechanical pass), search_musicbrainz_artist (existence check), verify_artists_on_recording (credit evidence), and flag_suspicious_artists (garble heuristics). A split is staged only when candidates exist on MusicBrainz and the credit evidence supports it; verified multi-artist values are staged with ; as separator.

docs.title: Docker Hosting and Two-Container Sandboxing
docs.text: MusicBee Tagger MCP supports a secure, least-privilege Docker Compose deployment utilizing a two-container sandboxing model. This architecture isolates the network-facing MCP server from the physical audio file modification agent.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Client["MCP Client / Claude"]
        CC["HTTPS Client"]
    end

    subgraph Container1["musicbee-mcp (Container 1)"]
        direction TB
        MCP["HTTPS MCP Server<br/>Read-only root fs<br/>Outbound: MusicBrainz only"]
    end

    subgraph Container2["musicbee-apply (Container 2)"]
        direction TB

    end

    subgraph Volumes["Docker Volumes & Mounts"]

    CC -->|HTTPS /mcp| MCP

    APPLY -->|rw| AUDIO
    APPLY -->|ro| STAGING
    APPLY --> DATA

docs.title: 1. musicbee-mcp (Container 1)
docs.text:
• Role: Exposes an HTTPS-secured Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on port 8443.
  • Security Posture:
  • Read-only root file system (read_only: true).
  • /audio directory mounted read-only (:ro) — enforces that the MCP server and AI agent can never modify physical audio files.
  • /staging (writable) for JSON stage manifests produced by the agent.
  • /data (writable) for persistent SQLite queue, job state, and token registrations.
  • Network access restricted to outbound calls required for MusicBrainz and ACRCloud APIs.

docs.title: 2. musicbee-apply (Container 2)
docs.text:
• Role: Executes physical audio tag modifications based on review-approved stage manifests.
  • Security Posture:
  • No outbound network access (musicbee-internal network without external gateway).
  • /audio directory mounted read-write (:rw) — the only container permitted to write to the library.
  • /staging mounted read-only (:ro) to read approved change manifests.

docs.title: Configuration & Deployment
docs.text:
1. Copy the environment template: 
    cp .env.example .env
  2. Configure .env to specify your local audio library path: 
    MUSICBEE_AUDIO_DIR=/path/to/your/music/library
MCP_HTTPS_PORT=8443
SECRET_COMMAND_TOKEN=your-secure-token
  3. Start the containers: 
    docker compose up -d
  4. Connect your MCP client (such as Claude Desktop) to https://localhost:8443/mcp.
  5. To apply review-approved staged changes: 
    docker compose exec musicbee-apply musicbee-tagger-apply --all

docs.title: Path Translation
docs.text: To bridge host filesystem paths with secure container bind mounts (e.g., mapping host library S:\Audio\Music\MusicBee\Main to container path /audio), the file registry uses virtual container path translation (translate_audio_path). This guarantees that token registration and staging operate correctly across host and container boundaries without exposing unmapped host paths to untrusted contexts.

docs.title: Local Desktop Release Plan
docs.text:
Purpose: Give a fresh coding agent enough context to prepare MusicBee Tagger MCP for reliable use on one Windows desktop.

Scope: Local Python package, Claude Code-style user configuration, K:\bin launcher, private local state, searchable investigation logs, and conservative confidence routing.

Not in scope: Docker, hosted/network MCP, PostgreSQL, multi-user support, or automatic writes to audio files.

docs.title: Product goal
docs.text: Make the MCP server easy to install and connect to Claude Code on the user's desktop, while keeping audio paths private and all physical audio edits under explicit user control.

docs.title: User preferences already gathered
docs.text:
• This is a single-user desktop tool.
  • The first target client is Claude Code, using a user-level configuration.
  • Install the Python application under: K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\
  • Put launchers or aliases in: K:\bin\
  • Prefer a Python package installation.
  • A human-run local command accepts playlist paths; the MCP server accepts only opaque file tokens.
  • Neither the agent nor ordinary MCP responses/logs should expose absolute paths.
  • Use a configurable private state/log root, set in the user-level MCP config. The requested default is: K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\
  • A Bash alias is acceptable if the MCP client can launch it reliably. On Windows, provide and test a native .cmd launcher as the dependable option.
  • Investigation summaries, staged proposals, applied changes, and unresolved searches should be recorded.
  • Confidence thresholds need validation against real examples and must remain configurable/tunable.

docs.title: Non-negotiable safety boundary
docs.text:
Auto-stage is not auto-apply.

  • The agent may inspect, search, verify, preview, log, and stage proposals.
  • The user-controlled CLI remains the only path that physically changes audio files in this plan.
  • Do not add an MCP tool that applies tags.
  • Any future request to let an agent apply audio changes requires a separate design and explicit approval. Do not infer that permission from confidence thresholds or logging requirements.

docs.title: 2. Current Project Starting Point
docs.text:
The repository already has:

  • An MCP server using stdio transport.
  • A Python console entry point: musicbee-tagger-mcp.
  • A separate user CLI: musicbee-tagger-apply.
  • Nine MCP tools for metadata inspection, MusicBrainz investigation, preview, staging, and mojibake repair; path-taking registration tools are not exposed.
  • Opaque tokens backed by a persistent, local token-to-path registry in the configured private data directory. A human-run CLI registers playlists and a separate confirmation-gated CLI clears registrations.
  • Metadata reads directly from audio files; metadata is not currently cached in a database.
  • Pending change manifests stored as JSON files.
  • A user CLI that prompts before writing tags and creates backups by default.
  • Tests for playlist parsing, path concealment, tag verification, staging, and MCP tool registration.

Recent structural refactor:

  • server.py assembles the app and starts stdio.
  • MCP handlers live in src/musicbee_tagger_mcp/tools/.
  • MusicBrainz search, verification, and shared scoring live in separate modules.
  • Manifest storage, read-only preview, staged application, and format-specific writes are separated.
  • The MCP server does not import the audio-write modules.

Before changing code, inspect the current branch and worktree. Do not assume the branch, line counts, or this plan's proposed module names remain unchanged.

docs.title: 3. Proposed Install Layout
docs.text:
Keep the executable environment, launcher, and application data clearly separated:

K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\
├── .venv\                 # Dedicated Python environment
├── pyproject.toml / package installation
├── staged\                # Pending change manifests
├── applied\               # Applied manifests and audit records
├── search-retry\          # Temporary/transient failures, retryable
├── search-archive\        # Completed unresolved investigations
├── low-confidence\        # Low-priority, user-browsable archive
└── logs\                  # Path-free event log

K:\bin\
├── musicbee-tagger-mcp.cmd
└── musicbee-tagger-mcp.sh   # Optional; only if supported/tested by the client shell

This is a proposed organization, not a settled on-disk schema. Confirm that the configured root can be both the install parent and data root without packaging/upgrades overwriting user data. If not, keep the requested root as the parent and place package/runtime files and private data in distinct subfolders.

docs.title: Launcher requirements
docs.text:
• The MCP config should call a stable command in K:\bin, not a checkout path.
  • Prefer a native .cmd launcher for Windows reliability.
  • The launcher should invoke the dedicated environment's installed console script.
  • Do not rely on the caller's current working directory.
  • A .sh launcher is optional and must be tested with the actual Claude Code shell.
  • Avoid baking credentials or user-specific secrets into launch scripts.

docs.title: Configuration requirements
docs.text:
• Use Claude Code's current supported user-level MCP configuration format. Verify the exact schema against current official documentation during implementation.
  • Configure the server command, arguments, and the private data-root setting.
  • Use the user's configured data root; default to K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\.
  • Do not add a config option that causes paths to be included in logs or MCP responses.
  • Document installation, config location, restart/reload behavior, and a health check.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
• Accept playlist paths only through a human-run local CLI, never through an MCP tool.
  • Resolve playlist-relative entries inside the server.
  • Use opaque tokens after registration.
  • Store token-to-path mappings in the configured private registration directory for token resolution across MCP restarts; the registration cleanup CLI removes these mappings after explicit confirmation.
  • This boundary keeps paths out of chat and MCP payloads, but is not protection from unrestricted same-user shell access.
  • Never include absolute paths in:
  • MCP tool responses
  • agent-facing notes
  • investigation logs
  • search archives
  • exception text shown to the agent
  • A bare filename/display name may be used as a human hint, but should not be treated as an identifier. Two files may share a name.
  • Review CLI output separately: show enough information for the user to identify a file, but do not print directory paths by default.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
• Continue reading tags from audio files on demand.
  • Do not introduce a metadata database merely to make the initial install work.
  • Consider metadata caching only after measuring a real performance issue.
  • Do not assume the filesystem is the bottleneck; separate tag reads, MusicBrainz requests, manifest writes, and audio writes in any benchmark.

docs.title: Private state root
docs.text:
Use the configured data root for private application state. Keep separate subfolders for:

  • pending stage manifests
  • applied stage/audit records
  • retryable search failures
  • completed unresolved searches
  • low-confidence investigation archive
  • concise append-only event logs

Create folders with restrictive user-only permissions where supported. On Windows, document how the user's profile/ACL controls access. Do not silently fall back to a public or shared temp directory for important records.

docs.title: 5. Confidence Routing Proposal
docs.text:
The current confidence value is a heuristic score, not a calibrated probability. Labels such as “95%” must not be described as a measured 95% chance of correctness.

Use these initial score bands for proposal routing only:

docs.title: 95–100 — Auto-stage
docs.text:
• Automatically create a pending stage proposal.
  • Log that it was auto-staged.
  • Still require all verification/evidence gates below.
  • Do not write the audio file. The user's CLI remains the apply gate.

docs.title: 85–94.9 — Corroborate, then agent judgment
docs.text:
• Perform web corroboration from reliable discographic sources.
  • Record concise source links and why they support or contradict the candidate.
  • The agent may stage only if evidence is coherent and the verifier has no important mismatch.
  • Otherwise archive as unresolved.

docs.title: 75–84.9 — Stage with an explicit caution
docs.text:
• A proposal may be staged for user review if the verifier passes.
  • Include a concise warning describing uncertainty or mismatched context.
  • Do not fill album/release/year fields based only on a recording match.

docs.title: 60–74.9 — Unresolved archive
docs.text:
• Do not stage.
  • Archive the candidate evidence for later investigation.
  • Add a short reason to the path-free log.

docs.title: <60 — Low-priority archive
docs.text:
• Do not stage.
  • Put the unresolved investigation in a user-browsable, low-priority archive.
  • This archive is a lower priority than the install, staging, and retry workflow.

docs.title: Hard gates override scores
docs.text:
No score band permits staging if:

  • verify_mbid does not return verified: true;
  • there is a material title, artist, or duration mismatch;
  • required evidence is missing or contradictory;
  • a match appears to be a different version (for example live vs studio) without adequate corroboration.

The exact threshold behavior, especially what evidence permits the 95+ route and what to do when MusicBrainz has no duration, must be tested and tuned before enabling auto-staging by default.

docs.title: Human-readable path-free log
docs.text:
Keep the ordinary log concise. Do not copy full API payloads into it.

Record:

  • registration/batch summary
  • auto-stage events
  • stage ID and path-free proposed-field summary
  • verifier score, duration difference, mismatch summary, and source links where relevant
  • unresolved outcomes and archive manifest IDs
  • apply attempts and outcomes
  • retryable API/network failures

docs.title: Applied-stage audit
docs.text:
For each apply attempt, write two linked events:

  1. Before: timestamp, event ID, stage ID, bare display name, fields proposed, and confirmation/apply intent.
  2. After: same event ID and stage ID, outcome, fields written, backup result, and concise error reason if failed.

Write the “before” record before attempting a physical write. Write the “after” record whether the operation succeeds or fails. Do not log the absolute path.

Current behavior is user CLI apply only. Preserve that. If agent application is ever authorized later, it must use the same before/after audit and receive a separate security design.

docs.title: Search failure and unresolved records
docs.text:
Distinguish these outcomes:

  • Transient failure: network error, rate limit, or service failure. Record a short reason and put a retryable manifest under search-retry.
  • Completed no-match: the API responded successfully, but no candidate passed investigation. Archive at the end of the batch under search-archive.
  • Low-confidence candidate: archive according to the score bands; do not mislabel it as a network failure.

The user asked for failed-search log entries to be two lines:

  1. a concise failure/no-match event with reason;
  2. the ID of the archived manifest.

Use a manifest ID rather than a path. The archive stays under the configured private data root.

docs.title: Minimum search manifest
docs.text:
Keep it small but sufficient to retry:

  • manifest ID and timestamp
  • path-free display name or batch-local token only if safe and meaningful
  • normalized artist/title/clue inputs used for the request
  • duration if available
  • query variant count
  • result count
  • concise outcome/reason
  • candidate recording IDs and scores if any were returned
  • source links if web research was performed
  • retry status / attempt count

Do not store audio paths, playlist paths, or raw exception messages that might include paths.

docs.title: 7. Delivery Phases
docs.text: Complete each phase independently. Keep changes small and testable.

docs.title: Phase 0 — Confirm assumptions and baseline
docs.text:
• [ ] Read .github/copilot-instructions.md, the investigator skill, this plan, and the user guide.
  • [ ] Confirm the worktree is clean and identify the target branch.
  • [ ] Run the current full test suite.
  • [ ] Inspect current package entry points, CLI behavior, MCP SDK version, and current Claude Code config schema.
  • [ ] Confirm the install/data folder layout does not put user data inside a directory replaced by upgrades.
  • [ ] Do not modify audio files during development tests.

Exit check: baseline tests pass and installation/config schema is documented from current official guidance.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Install package and launcher
docs.text:
• [ ] Create a reproducible install into the dedicated location under K:\tools\mcp-servers\musicbee-tags\.
  • [ ] Add a native K:\bin\musicbee-tagger-mcp.cmd launcher.
  • [ ] Add a Bash launcher only if the user's Claude Code environment requires and supports it.
  • [ ] Ensure the launcher works from a different current directory.
  • [ ] Verify the configured package command starts the existing stdio MCP server.
  • [ ] Add a user-level Claude Code config example using the stable launcher.

Exit check: clean install and MCP initialize/tool-list smoke test succeed without requiring the source checkout.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Private data root and durable folders
docs.text:
• [ ] Read the configurable data root from user-level MCP environment/config.
  • [ ] Use the requested default root unless install/data separation requires subfolders.
  • [ ] Create stage, applied, retry, archive, low-confidence, and log folders on demand.
  • [ ] Handle unavailable folders with explicit, path-sanitized errors; never silently lose state.
  • [ ] Ensure a restart preserves pending stages and archives.

Exit check: state survives server restart, remains local, and no path appears in MCP responses or logs.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Structured event log and manifests
docs.text:
• [ ] Define versioned, append-only path-free log records.
  • [ ] Log auto-stage events and link each record to a stage ID.
  • [ ] Implement before/after apply events with the same event ID.
  • [ ] Separate retryable transient failures from completed no-match searches.
  • [ ] Archive no-match investigations at batch end, as requested.
  • [ ] Make archive manifests retryable without re-registering files or requiring old tokens.
  • [ ] Add safe retention/cleanup guidance; do not automatically delete user records.

Exit check: tests prove event pairing, path concealment, restart/retry behavior, and failure visibility.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Confidence routing
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep the current verifier as a hard evidence gate.
  • [ ] Add an explicit, testable routing function for the proposed score bands.
  • [ ] Require web corroboration for the 85–94.9 band before agent-judged staging.
  • [ ] Include an uncertainty note for the 75–84.9 band.
  • [ ] Archive 60–74.9 and below-60 outcomes without staging.
  • [ ] Require no major mismatch even for scores at or above 95.
  • [ ] Add tests for every boundary: 59.9, 60, 74.9, 75, 84.9, 85, 94.9, and 95.
  • [ ] Keep the feature disabled or conservative by default until evaluated against a representative set of matches.

Exit check: boundary tests and a labeled evaluation set demonstrate that score routing does not bypass verification.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Documentation and release checks
docs.text:
• [ ] Update the user guide with install, config, launcher, data folders, logs, retry, and CLI apply instructions.
  • [ ] Update the investigator skill with the finalized confidence routing and archive behavior.
  • [ ] Document backup/restore and uninstall behavior without deleting user data.
  • [ ] Run the full test suite, package build/install smoke test, config parse/launch smoke test, and git diff --check.
  • [ ] Confirm MCP tool inventory is unchanged unless an explicitly reviewed feature requires a change.
  • [ ] Confirm MCP imports still cannot reach the physical audio write implementation.
  • [ ] Commit each coherent, tested phase; do not amend existing commits.

Exit check: another person can install and configure the server from the guide without opening the repository's source code.

docs.title: Install and config
docs.text:
• [ ] Package installs into the dedicated Python environment.
  • [ ] K:\bin launcher works from PowerShell and from the MCP client.
  • [ ] MCP config validates and launches stdio.
  • [ ] Failure messages are useful but do not echo absolute paths.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
• [ ] MCP responses never return audio or playlist paths.
  • [ ] Logs and search manifests never contain absolute paths.
  • [ ] Pending stage manifests keep path information private and are readable only by the local apply workflow.
  • [ ] Duplicate filenames do not cause stage/search records to be confused.

docs.title: Routing and logs
docs.text:
• [ ] Every confidence boundary is tested.
  • [ ] Failed verification never stages regardless of score.
  • [ ] Auto-stage emits a log record and still does not modify audio.
  • [ ] Apply writes a before record and an after record, including on failure.
  • [ ] Retryable errors and completed no-match outcomes are stored separately.
  • [ ] Archived searches can be retried later from their path-free inputs.

docs.title: Audio safety
docs.text:
• [ ] MCP tool listing contains no apply/write tool.
  • [ ] MCP server process does not import audio-write modules.
  • [ ] Only explicit CLI confirmation performs physical tag changes.
  • [ ] Tests use generated temporary audio fixtures or mocks, never the user's library.

docs.title: 9. New-Agent Handoff Instructions
docs.text:
The next agent should:

  1. Read this plan, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .agents/skills/musicbee-investigator/SKILL.md, and docs/index.html.
  2. Inspect the current branch, commit, worktree, test commands, and package entry points before editing.
  3. Treat all preferences above as requirements unless explicitly marked “proposed” or “to validate.”
  4. Implement only one delivery phase at a time.
  5. Ask before changing the no-agent-audio-writes boundary.
  6. Never send audio/playlist paths to a subagent. If delegating, pass path-free briefs and verify shared MCP token access first.
  7. Use web research for weak or conflicting MusicBrainz matches; retain citations in the appropriate record.
  8. Update WORK_LOG.md after substantive work and commit coherent verified changes with the required Copilot co-author trailer.
  9. Report what changed, tests run, remaining risks, and any user decision needed.

docs.title: 10. Open Decisions to Validate During Implementation
docs.text:
• Does the install root double as the data root, or should state live in a child folder such as data\ to protect it during upgrades?
  • Which user-level Claude Code config format/version is installed on the target desktop?
  • Should the .sh launcher be implemented, or is .cmd sufficient for the actual client?
  • What test corpus is representative enough to tune heuristic confidence thresholds?
  • Does “85–94.9 agent judgment” always require a web citation, or can another documented independent source count?
  • How long should applied manifests, retryable failures, and low-confidence archives be retained?
  • Is display-name logging acceptable for the user's privacy expectations, or should logs use only opaque IDs?
  • What happens when no local duration or MusicBrainz duration is available? Recommended default: no auto-stage.
  • Keep all actual audio writes user-confirmed by CLI. Any change to that rule needs an explicit, separate approval.

docs.title: OpenRouter Agent Loop
docs.text: A model-driven batch agent that wraps the MusicBee Tagger MCP tools. It processes audio files in batches of 10, using OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint with function calling.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. A playlist job is created by the human-run registration CLI — only opaque tokens, a job id, and bare filenames ever reach the model (same privacy model as the MCP server). The MCP list_jobs tool shows path-free summaries for jobs with pending tracks. If exactly one job is available, the loop selects it automatically; otherwise pass a job id.
  2. The agent claims batches of up to 10 unprocessed tokens via next_batch.
  3. The loop sends a batch brief (existing tags, durations, filename clues) to the model with a system prompt adapted from the musicbee-investigator skill.
  4. The model decides which tools to call. The loop executes them locally:
  5. inspection: read_track_metadata, extract_filename_clues, get_batch_brief
  6. identity: search_canonical_release, verify_mbid (the mandatory gate), identify_acrcloud, web_search
  7. text: repair_mojibake
  8. artist splits: propose_artist_split, search_musicbrainz_artist, verify_artists_on_recording, flag_suspicious_artists
  9. staging: preview_tags, stage_tag_changes (manifest only — no audio writes)
  10. batch/queue: next_batch, complete_batch, release_batch, job_status, list_jobs, enqueue_batch_operation, list_batch_operations, update_batch_operation
  11. A verified recording is required by the local harness before it permits stage_tag_changes. Failed verification can be retried or explicitly marked unresolved.
  12. Each finish_batch is checked against all batch tokens. Outcomes are recorded with complete_batch; model/API errors are logged and claimed work is completed as failed rather than left in progress.
  13. A JSON state file records progress. A path-sanitized JSONL log records batch briefs, visible model summaries, tool calls/results, timing, and errors. OpenRouter does not expose hidden chain-of-thought; logs contain only user-visible summaries and tool activity.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
pip install musicbee-tagger-mcp  # or run from a source checkout
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
python scripts/openrouter_agent_loop.py [job_id] \
    --model openrouter/free --batch-size 10 --max-batches 3 --max-turns 15 \
    --debug --resume

Context compaction is on by default and trims failures, failure mentions and repeated messages from the history mid-run; --compaction-model runs that summarisation through a separate (typically cheaper) OpenRouter model, and --no-compact-context disables compaction entirely. --context-chars bounds how much of each tool result stays in context and --thought-tokens bounds the visible summary budget.

Logs default to the private application data directory's agent_logs folder. --max-consecutive-incomplete (default 3; use 0 to disable) controls how many incomplete batches may occur before stuck tracks are skipped; otherwise released tracks are retried on later iterations. --debug pauses before claiming a batch, submitting metadata to OpenRouter, each model turn, and each stage operation; press Enter to continue or q to stop at that checkpoint. Without --debug, no pause prompts occur.

Omit job_id when exactly one job has pending tracks. If multiple jobs are available, the script lists their IDs and asks you to specify one. Use the MCP list_jobs tool to inspect available jobs without exposing paths or track tokens.

docs.title: Model choice
docs.text: Any OpenRouter model works (openrouter/free is the default). The system prompt is model-agnostic; tool calls follow the standard OpenAI function-calling format. Alias slugs like ~openai/gpt-sol-latest always resolve to the newest model in a family.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Do not run shell commands (bash, cmd, powershell, python, etc.) without first making absolutely sure that the required action cannot be performed using an existing exposed tool (MCP tool, skill, or other available tool). Prefer the exposed tool; use a shell only as a last resort and state why no exposed tool can do it.

  • Staging never writes audio files. Apply still requires the separate apply_staged CLI with interactive confirmation and backups.

  • The batch brief sends filenames and existing tag metadata to the selected OpenRouter model. The local JSONL run log stays in the configured data directory unless --log supplies another path.
  • Unknown tokens, invalid arguments, and unknown tool names return errors to the model rather than raising.
  • Tool results are truncated to 6 KB per message to bound context growth.

docs.title: Concurrency and recovery
docs.text:
JobStore serializes reads and writes for one data directory with a cross-process file lock (.jobs.lock in the jobs directory). Multiple openrouter_agent_loop.py processes, MCP servers, or CLI commands sharing a data directory therefore cannot claim the same pending tokens, and complete_batch/release_batch updates are not lost.

  • next_batch claims tokens atomically under the lock; a second process sees the updated in_progress statuses and skips them.
  • Writes are persisted atomically (temporary file + replace) to avoid partial job files.
  • Interrupted or failed runs can be recovered by calling release_batch for the affected tokens (returns them to pending, moving them to the end of the queue) or by restarting the agent loop with --resume, which releases stuck in-progress tokens from the previous run before claiming new work.

If a process is killed while holding the lock, the operating system releases the file lock automatically; the job file remains consistent because writes are atomic.

docs.title: Costs
docs.text: A batch of 10 files typically needs 15-40 tool-call turns; with a small model this is well under USD 0.05 per batch. Check current pricing at https://openrouter.ai/models.

docs.title: Generic agent entry point and Cline backend
docs.text:
The shared entry point scripts/agent_loop_script.py (also available as scripts/agent_loop.py and scripts/agent.py) selects a backend with --agent / --agent-type / --backend:

# Built-in OpenRouter / OpenAI-style function calling (default)
python scripts/agent_loop_script.py --agent openrouter [job_id]

# Local Cline installation (npm install -g cline)
python scripts/agent_loop_script.py --agent cline [job_id]

The Cline backend delegates to a locally installed cline executable. Install and authenticate it first:

npm i -g cline
cline auth

Cline is given the MusicBee Tagger MCP tools through its MCP configuration and uses the same opaque-token, path-free workflow as the OpenRouter backend. The OpenRouter backend remains the default and uses OpenAI-style function calling.

docs.title: Threat Model and Path-Handling Decision
docs.text: Status: decided. This documents the security decision required by issue #3 ("registration: MCP tool or human-run CLI") and the trust boundaries the code implements. Read this before changing anything in file_registry.py, tools/files.py, staging.py, or stage_manifest_store.py.

docs.title: Deployment context
docs.text:
• Single user, single Windows desktop, private repository.
  • The MCP server talks to one agent over stdio on the same machine.
  • No network exposure: no hosted MCP, no Docker, no multi-user mode.

docs.title: Actors and trust levels
docs.text: Actor Trust level Can do Human user Full trust Runs CLIs, edits audio, approves applies MCP agent (e.g. Claude Code) Untrusted for paths Calls MCP tools with tokens only Config / registry files on disk Human-owned Readable by anything the user can read

docs.title: Core decision: registration is a human-run CLI, not an MCP tool
docs.text:
Path-taking registration is NOT exposed as an MCP operation. The MCP server exposes no tool that accepts a filesystem path. Registration happens only through musicbee-tagger-register (playlist CLI), which the user runs in a separate terminal.

Rationale:

  1. The user chooses which files enter the workspace; the agent cannot add arbitrary files by supplying paths.
  2. Path-free by construction: no MCP request ever contains a path, so no tool error, log line, or serialization can leak one from registration.
  3. An allowed-root check (canonically resolving and confining paths) is unnecessary for MCP because MCP never receives paths. The playlist CLI already rejects unsupported formats and unresolvable entries, and every error path returns a message without the entry path.

If registration ever becomes an MCP tool, this decision must be revisited with an allowed-root config, resolve()-then-containment checks, symlink and traversal rejection, and extension allowlisting. Do not make that change casually.

docs.title: Attack surface and mitigations
docs.text: Concern Status Paths in MCP responses Mitigated — tokens and bare display names only; file_path keys popped before return Paths in MCP error text Mitigated — tool handlers catch exceptions and return path-free messages; read_audio_metadata raises path-free errors Paths in MCP logs / serialization Mitigated — server emits only tool results; nothing path-bearing is in the response payload Agent reading the registry directly Not mitigated (accepted) — the agent runs on the same user account and holds whatever filesystem rights the user has. The registry stores absolute paths under the private data directory. A truly hostile agent with shell access is out of scope: it could read any user file regardless Token guessing Mitigated — tokens are UUIDv4, validated with strict UUID parsing before lookup Token replay across restarts By design — the persistent registry lets tokens survive restarts; the user clears registrations via the confirmation-gated clear CLI Staged manifests Accepted — staged/*.json contains absolute_path on disk so the human CLI can apply; the MCP list_pending() view returns path-free summaries only Playlist entries escaping intent Mitigated — only .m3u/.m3u8, audio extensions only, remote entries rejected, per-entry path-free skip reasons Prompt injection via tags/filenames Accepted — an agent could read malicious tag text; it cannot write audio without the human CLI, which prompts before applying

docs.title: Residual risk (explicitly accepted)
docs.text:
• A malicious or compromised agent with unrestricted shell access can read the registry, the manifests, and the audio files directly. This equals the user's own privileges and is inherent to a local desktop agent; nothing short of OS-level sandboxing changes it.
  • Display names (filename stems) are shown to the agent. Filenames may contain sensitive wording; this is intentional and required for the investigation workflow.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• tests/ covers path concealment, playlist parsing, staging summaries, and registry persistence, including Windows-style absolute paths.
  • Adding or changing an MCP tool requires: no path parameter, no path in the return value, no path in any error branch, and a test proving it.

def cmd_revert_one(applier, stage_id: str) -> str:
    """Revert an applied staged change by restoring its .bak backup."""
    try:
        manifest = applier.load(stage_id)
    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
        logger.error("Staged manifest %s is missing; cannot revert.", stage_id)
        print(f"\n[ERROR] Stage {stage_id} is missing.")
        return "missing_stage"
    if not manifest.get("applied"):
        status = []
        if manifest.get("reverted"):
            status.append("already reverted")
        if manifest.get("withdrawn"):
            status.append("withdrawn")
        if manifest.get("failed"):
            status.append("failed")
        if manifest.get("archived"):
            status.append("archived")
        print(f"\n[SKIP] {stage_id} is {', '.join(status) or 'not applied'}; cannot revert.")
        return "not_applied"
    backup_path = manifest.get("backup_path")
    if not backup_path:
        print(f"\n[SKIP] {stage_id} has no backup path stored; cannot revert.")
        return "no_backup"
    backup = Path(backup_path)
    if not backup.is_file():
        print("\n[ERROR] Backup file not found; cannot revert.")
        return "no_backup_file"

    display_name = manifest.get("display_name", stage_id)
    print()
    print(f"Revert preview for {stage_id}:")
    print(f"  file: {display_name}")
    print(f"  backup: {backup_path}")
    print()
    print("This will restore the original .bak backup over the current file,")
    print("undoing all tag changes that were applied.")
    answer = input(
        "\nEnter=revert/restore backup, q=quit [Enter/q]: "
    ).strip().lower()
    if answer == "q":
        print("Quitting revert.")
        return "quit"
    if answer not in {"", "y", "yes"}:
        print("Unrecognized choice; revert aborted.")
        return "pending"

    try:
        result = applier.revert(stage_id)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        logger.error("Revert failed for %s: %s", stage_id, exc)
        print("\n[ERROR] Revert failed: file not found.")
        return "error"
    if result.get("status") == "already_reverted":
        print(f"\n[SKIP] {stage_id} has already been reverted.")
        return "already_reverted"
    print(f"\n✓ Reverted {stage_id}: {display_name}")
    print(f"  Restored from backup: {backup_path}")
    return "reverted"

def run(
    input_stream: TextIO = sys.stdin,
    output_stream: TextIO = sys.stdout,
    playlist_path: str = "",
) -> int:
    """Register a supplied playlist or prompt locally, then print path-free details."""
    print(
        "This local command registers playlist entries without sending paths to "
        "the MCP agent.",
        file=output_stream,
    )
    print(
        "Run this command in a separate terminal, not through the agent.",
        file=output_stream,
    )
    if not playlist_path:
        print(
            "Playlist path (.m3u or .m3u8): ",
            end="",
            file=output_stream,
            flush=True,
        )
        playlist_path = input_stream.readline().strip().strip('"')
    if not playlist_path:
        print("No playlist path was entered.", file=output_stream)
        return 1

    playlist_name = playlist_path.replace("\\", "/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    job_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    get_job_store().create_job([], playlist_name=playlist_name, skipped=0, job_id=job_id)
    print(
        f"Job id: {job_id} (registration in progress)",
        file=output_stream,
        flush=True,
    )

    result = register_playlist(
        playlist_path,
        get_registry(),
        get_job_store(),
        job_id,
        progress_callback=lambda current, total: _progress_bar(
            output_stream, current, total
        ),
    )
    if "error" in result:
        print(f"Unable to register playlist: {result['error']}.", file=output_stream)
        return 1

    registered_count = len(result["registered"])
    print(
        f"Registered {registered_count} audio file(s) as playlist job "
        f"{job_id}.",
        file=output_stream,
    )
    duplicates = result.get("duplicates", [])
    if duplicates:
        count = len(duplicates)
        label = "entry" if count == 1 else "entries"
        print(
            f"Skipped {count} duplicate playlist {label} already registered "
            f"in another active job:",
            file=output_stream,
        )
        for entry in duplicates:
            print(
                f"- {entry.get('display_name')}: existing job "
                f"{entry.get('existing_job_id')}",
                file=output_stream,
            )
    print(
        "Pass this job id to the agent loop or ask the agent for the next "
        "batch; the playlist path was never sent over MCP.",
        file=output_stream,
    )

    skipped = result["skipped"]
    if skipped:
        count = len(skipped)
        label = "entry" if count == 1 else "entries"
        print(f"Skipped {count} playlist {label}:", file=output_stream)
        for entry in skipped:
            print(f"- Line {entry['line']}: {entry['error']}", file=output_stream)

    try:
        groups = get_job_store().album_groups(job_id)
        group_count = groups.get("group_count", 0) if isinstance(groups, dict) else 0
        if group_count:
            print(f"Album groups: {group_count}", file=output_stream)
            for group in groups.get("album_groups", []):
                print(
                    f"- {group.get('album')}: {group.get('track_count', 0)} track(s)",
                    file=output_stream,
                )
        single_count = groups.get("single_count", 0) if isinstance(groups, dict) else 0
        if single_count:
            print(f"Single-track items: {single_count}", file=output_stream)
    except Exception:
        pass

    return 0

class AuditReport(list):
    """Audit report that is primarily a list of flagged stages.

    Mapping-style access is delegated to the full report dictionary, so callers
    that expect either a list or a dict can use the same object.
    """

    def __init__(self, flagged, report):
        super().__init__(flagged)
        self._report = dict(report)

    def _mapping(self):
        return self._report

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        if isinstance(key, str):
            return self._report[key]
        return super().__getitem__(key)

    def __contains__(self, key):
        if isinstance(key, str):
            return key in self._report
        return super().__contains__(key)

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        if isinstance(key, str):
            return self._report.get(key, default)
        return default

    def keys(self):
        return self._report.keys()

    def values(self):
        return self._report.values()

    def items(self):
        return self._report.items()

    def __repr__(self):
        return repr(self._report)

class StagingManager:
    """Manages pending tag-change manifests on disk."""

    def __init__(self, staging_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> None:
        self.store = StageManifestStore(staging_dir)
        self.staging_dir = self.store.directory

    def stage(
        self,
        absolute_path: Path,
        display_name: str,
        proposed_tags: Dict[str, Any],
        mb_recording_id: Optional[str] = None,
        mb_release_id: Optional[str] = None,
        forensic_score: Optional[float] = None,
        match_source: Optional[str] = None,
        match_confidence: Optional[float] = None,
        notes: str = "",
        token: Optional[str] = None,
        job_id: Optional[str] = None,
        batch: Optional[str] = None,
        note: Optional[str] = None,
        rationale: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Write a pending change manifest and return a stage_id + summary.

        The absolute_path is stored inside the manifest file on disk.
        It is NEVER returned to the caller.

        Returns:
            {"stage_id": str, "display_name": str, "diff_summary": list, "notes": str}
        """
        # Generate the field-by-field diff (reads file for current values).
        diff = _changed_fields(str(absolute_path), proposed_tags)
        try:
            baseline_tags = read_audio_metadata(str(absolute_path)).get("tags", {})
        except Exception:
            baseline_tags = None

        override_text = (
            manual_override_justification
            or override_justification
            or override_reason
            or justification
        )
        is_manual_override = bool(manual_override or override_text)
        if is_manual_override:
            if not isinstance(override_text, str) or not override_text.strip():
                raise ValueError("justification is required for a manual override")
            override_text = override_text.strip()
        else:
            override_text = None

        if not notes and note:
            notes = note
        if rationale:
            notes = (str(notes).strip() + ", " + str(rationale).strip()).strip() if notes else str(rationale).strip()
        notes = notes if isinstance(notes, str) else ("" if notes is None else str(notes))

        stage_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        manifest = {
            "stage_id": stage_id,
            "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "previous_tags": baseline_tags,
            "display_name": display_name,
            "absolute_path": str(absolute_path),  # stored on disk, never returned
            "token": token,
            "job_id": job_id,
            "batch": batch,
            "proposed_tags": proposed_tags,
            "diff": diff,
            "mb_recording_id": mb_recording_id,
            "mb_release_id": mb_release_id,
            "forensic_score": forensic_score,
            "match_source": match_source,
            "match_confidence": match_confidence,
            "notes": notes,
            "note": notes,
            "rationale": notes,
            "applied": False,
            "withdrawn": False,
            "revision": 1,
            "history": [],

    def _validate_mbid(field: str, value: str) -> None:
        try:
            uuid.UUID(value.strip())
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{field} must be a MusicBrainz UUID or empty to clear it."
            ) from None

    @staticmethod
    def _status(manifest: dict) -> str:
        if manifest.get("applied"):
            return "applied"
        if manifest.get("withdrawn"):
            return "withdrawn"
        if manifest.get("archived"):
            return "archived"
        if manifest.get("failed"):

        return "pending"

        status = cls._status(manifest)
        if status != "pending":

            )

def stage(
    self,
    absolute_path: Path,
    display_name: str,
    proposed_tags: Dict[str, Any],
    mb_recording_id: Optional[str] = None,
    mb_release_id: Optional[str] = None,
    forensic_score: Optional[float] = None,
    match_source: Optional[str] = None,
    match_confidence: Optional[float] = None,
    notes: str = "",
    token: Optional[str] = None,
    job_id: Optional[str] = None,
    batch: Optional[str] = None,
    note: Optional[str] = None,
    rationale: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict:
    """Write a pending change manifest and return a stage_id + summary.

    The absolute_path is stored inside the manifest file on disk.
    It is NEVER returned to the caller.

    Returns:
        {"stage_id": str, "display_name": str, "diff_summary": list, "notes": str}
    """
    # Generate the field-by-field diff (reads file for current values).
    diff = _changed_fields(str(absolute_path), proposed_tags)
    try:
        baseline_tags = read_audio_metadata(str(absolute_path)).get("tags", {})
    except Exception:
        baseline_tags = None

    override_text = (
        manual_override_justification
        or override_justification
        or override_reason
        or justification
    )
    is_manual_override = bool(manual_override or override_text)
    if is_manual_override:
        if not isinstance(override_text, str) or not override_text.strip():
            raise ValueError("justification is required for a manual override")
        override_text = override_text.strip()
    else:
        override_text = None

    if not notes and note:
        notes = note
    if rationale:
        notes = (str(notes).strip() + ", " + str(rationale).strip()).strip() if notes else str(rationale).strip()
    notes = notes if isinstance(notes, str) else ("" if notes is None else str(notes))

    stage_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    manifest = {
        "stage_id": stage_id,
        "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "previous_tags": baseline_tags,
        "display_name": display_name,
        "absolute_path": str(absolute_path),  # stored on disk, never returned
        "token": token,
        "job_id": job_id,
        "batch": batch,
        "proposed_tags": proposed_tags,
        "diff": diff,
        "mb_recording_id": mb_recording_id,
        "mb_release_id": mb_release_id,
        "forensic_score": forensic_score,
        "match_source": match_source,
        "match_confidence": match_confidence,
        "notes": notes,
        "note": notes,
        "rationale": notes,
        "applied": False,
        "withdrawn": False,
        "revision": 1,
        "history": [],
    }

    if is_manual_override:
        manifest.setdefault("history", []).append({
            "action": "manual_override",
            "at": manifest["created_at"],
            "reason": override_text,
        })

    self.store.save(manifest)

    # Return only safe, non-path fields to the caller
    return {
        "stage_id": stage_id,
        "display_name": display_name,
        "revision": 1,
        "diff_summary": diff,
        "notes": notes,
        "message": (
            f"Staged {len(diff)} field change(s) for '{display_name}'. "
            f"Run `python -m musicbee_tagger_mcp.apply_staged --stage-id {stage_id}` to apply."
        ),
    }

class FileRegistry:
    """Token-to-path store with optional persistence for local registration.

    Persistent registries let a human-run local command register files before
    the MCP client starts, without sending paths in MCP tool calls.
    """

    def __init__(self, directory: Optional[Path] = None) -> None:
        self.directory = directory
        self._store: Dict[str, Path] = {}  # token → absolute path

    def register(self, path: str, store_path: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
        """Register a file path and return a token + display name.

        Verifies existence of `path` on disk, but optionally persists `store_path`
        (e.g., container virtual path).

        Returns:
            {"token": str, "display_name": str}
            display_name is the bare filename only — never a path.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: if the path does not exist on disk.
        """
        p = Path(str(path)).expanduser().resolve()
        if not p.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError("File not found")
        s = Path(str(store_path)) if store_path else p
        existing = self.token_for_path(s)
        if existing is not None:
            return {"token": existing, "display_name": p.name,
                    "already_registered": True}
        token = str(uuid.uuid4())
        self._store[token] = s
        if self.directory is not None:
            self._save(token, s)
        return {"token": token, "display_name": p.name}

    def register_many(self, paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
        """Register a list of paths. Returns list of {token, display_name}."""
        return [self.register(p) for p in paths]

    def resolve(self, token: str) -> Path:
        """Resolve a token to its absolute path (internal use only).

        Raises:
            KeyError: if the token is not registered.
        """
        try:
            normalized_token = str(uuid.UUID(token))
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            # Support the short aliases shown to agents when they uniquely
            # identify one registered token.  This keeps read_track_metadata and
            # related tools usable if a caller passes an abbreviated token.
            candidates = self._matching_tokens(token)
            if len(candidates) == 1:
                normalized_token = next(iter(candidates))
            else:
                raise KeyError("Unknown file token") from None

        if normalized_token in self._store:
            return self._store[normalized_token]
        if self.directory is None:
            raise KeyError("Unknown file token")

        record_path = self.directory / f"{normalized_token}.json"
        try:
            record = json.loads(record_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            path = Path(record["path"])
            if record["token"] != normalized_token or not _is_absolute_path(path):
                raise ValueError
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            raise KeyError("Unknown file token") from None

        self._store[normalized_token] = path
        return path

    def _matching_tokens(self, prefix: str) -> set[str]:
        """Return registered full tokens uniquely matching a short prefix."""
        if not isinstance(prefix, str) or len(prefix.strip()) < 4:
            return set()
        needle = prefix.strip().lower()
        candidates: set[str] = set()
        for token in self._store:
            if token.lower().startswith(needle):
                candidates.add(token)
        if self.directory is not None:
            for record_path in self.directory.glob("*.json"):
                try:
                    token = str(uuid.UUID(record_path.stem))
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                if token.lower().startswith(needle):
                    candidates.add(token)
        return candidates


    def token_for_path(self, path: Path | str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Return the token already registered for this path, if any."""
        path_str = str(path)
        resolved = Path(path) if path_str.startswith("/") else Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
        for token, registered in self._store.items():
            if registered == resolved:
                return token
        if self.directory is not None:
            for record_path in self.directory.glob("*.json"):
                try:
                    token = str(uuid.UUID(record_path.stem))
                    record = json.loads(record_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                    rec_path = Path(record["path"])
                    if token not in self._store and rec_path == resolved:
                        self._store[token] = resolved
                        return token
                except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
                    continue
        return None

    def is_registered(self, token: str) -> bool:
        try:
            self.resolve(token)
        except KeyError:
            return False
        return True

    def revoke(self, token: str) -> None:
        """Remove a token from the registry (e.g. after staging is applied)."""
        try:
            normalized_token = str(uuid.UUID(token))
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            return
        self._store.pop(normalized_token, None)
        if self.directory is not None:
            (self.directory / f"{normalized_token}.json").unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def list_tokens(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return all registered tokens with their display names (no paths)."""
        entries = {
            token: {"token": token, "display_name": path.name}
            for token, path in self._store.items()
        }
        if self.directory is not None:
            for record_path in self.directory.glob("*.json"):
                try:
                    token = str(uuid.UUID(record_path.stem))
                    record = json.loads(record_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                    path = Path(record["path"])
                    if record["token"] == token and _is_absolute_path(path):
                        entries[token] = {"token": token, "display_name": path.name}
                except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
                    continue
        return list(entries.values())

    def clear(self) -> int:
        """Delete persisted registrations and return their count."""
        count = len(self.list_tokens())
        self._store.clear()
        if self.directory is not None:
            for record_path in self.directory.glob("*.json"):
                record_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return count

    def _save(self, token: str, path: Path) -> None:
        """Atomically save one token mapping without exposing its path."""
        temporary_path = None
        try:
            self.directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
                "w",
                encoding="utf-8",
                dir=self.directory,
                delete=False,
                suffix=".tmp",
            ) as temporary:
                json.dump({"token": token, "path": str(path)}, temporary)
                temporary_path = Path(temporary.name)
            os.replace(temporary_path, self.directory / f"{token}.json")
        except OSError:
            if temporary_path is not None:
                try:
                    temporary_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                except OSError:
                    pass
            self._store.pop(token, None)
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Unable to save local registration; check the data directory "
                "and local permissions."
            ) from None

def preview_tag_changes(file_path: str, new_tags: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a field-by-field diff without writing to the audio file."""
    current_tags = read_audio_metadata(file_path).get("tags", {})
    diff = {}
    invisible_fields = []
    for key in sorted(set(current_tags) | set(new_tags)):
        before = current_tags.get(key)
        after = new_tags.get(key, before)
        changed = (
            str(before) if before is not None else ""
        ) != (
            str(after) if after is not None else ""
        ) and key in new_tags
        diff[key] = {
            "before": before,
            "after": after if key in new_tags else before,
            "changed": changed,
            "invisible_chars_omitted": _has_invisible(before) or _has_invisible(after),
        }
        if _has_invisible(before) or _has_invisible(after):
            invisible_fields.append(key)
    return {
        "file_path": file_path,
        "has_changes": any(item["changed"] for item in diff.values()),
        "diff": diff,
        "invisible_chars_omitted": bool(invisible_fields),
        "fields_with_invisible_chars": invisible_fields,
    }

def apply_tags_to_file(
    file_path: str,
    new_tags: Dict[str, Any],
    create_backup: bool = True,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Write proposed tags after optional backup creation."""
    path = Path(file_path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}")

    preview = preview_tag_changes(file_path, new_tags)
    if not preview["has_changes"]:
        return {
            "file_path": file_path,
            "status": "skipped",
            "message": "No changes detected",
            "backup_created": False,
        }

    audio = mutagen.File(file_path)
    if audio is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {file_path}")

    backup_path = None
    if create_backup:
        backup_path = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".bak")
        shutil.copy2(path, backup_path)

    if hasattr(audio, "tags") and (isinstance(audio.tags, ID3) or path.suffix.lower() == ".mp3"):
        write_id3(audio, new_tags)
    elif isinstance(audio, (FLAC, OggVorbis)):
        write_vorbis(audio, new_tags)
    elif isinstance(audio, MP4):
        write_mp4(audio, new_tags)
    else:
        for key, value in new_tags.items():
            if value is not None:
                audio[key] = [str(value)]
        audio.save()

    return {
        "file_path": file_path,
        "status": "success",
        "backup_created": str(backup_path) if backup_path else None,
        "fields_written": [key for key, change in preview["diff"].items()
                           if change["changed"]],
        "applied_diff": preview["diff"],
    }
